newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on USDA stocks cut. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on USDA stocks cut. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]

text.p: A cut by USDA in its outlook for 1996-97 U.S. soybean ending stocks boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"The supply/demand was a surprise for beans, the fact they increased exports 30 million bushels (Corrects from tonnes) was a surprise," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

USDA reduced to 180 million bushels its forecast for U.S. soybean carryover for the 1996-97 marketing year which ends on August 31, 1997. The November supply/demand report had pegged the carryover at 210 million. A 30 million bushel increase in estimated exports of U.S. soy trimmed the carryout estimate.

Soybeans also found support from the government's weekly export sales data released Thursday that showed U.S. net export sales of soybeans for the week ended December 5 at 645,400 tonnes. That tally was above trade expectations for 450,000 to 550,000 tonnes.
Technical traders said the close Thursday was bullish as January ended above resistance at the $7.00 per bushel mark.
"The technical picture looks better and the fundamental news was supportive," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Soybeans closed five to 12-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with January up 11-1/4 at $7.02-3/4.
Traders also said there was talk during the trading session that China bought soymeal and soybeans from the U.S.
Refco Inc bought five million bushels of March, Tenco Inc bought 1.7 million bushels of January and Cargill Investor Services bought three million bushels of March, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 54,000 contracts, above the 48,272 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Smith Barney bought 500 March $7.00 calls and sold 500 March $7.25 calls at 7-1/2 cents, Term Commodities bought 500 January $6.75 puts at 7/8 cent and Refco Inc bought 400 March $7.25 puts, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, above the 12,914 traded Wednesday.
